<div class="about-text">

I am a Postdoctoral Researcher in the [School of Social Sciences and Government at the Tecnológico de Monterrey](https://tec.mx/en/our-faculty/ecsg).

I hold a PhD in Applied Statistics and Empirical Methods from the [Georg-August-Universität Göttingen](https://www.uni-goettingen.de/), completed in 2022 with the _summa cum laude_ distinction. My [PhD dissertation](https://ediss.uni-goettingen.de/handle/11858/14585?locale-attribute=en) focused on developing [boosting structured additive regression models](https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-662-63882-8_9) to address critical issues in development economics.

Before pursuing my doctoral studies, I earned a bachelor's degree in Economics from the [Universidad Autónoma de Coahuila](https://www.uadec.mx/) and a master's degree in Applied Statistics from the [Tecnológico de Monterrey](https://tec.mx/en/our-faculty/ecsg).

Currently, I also contribute as a Research Data Analyst to the [Internal Displacement Monitoring Centre (IDMC)](https://www.internal-displacement.org/) of the [Norwegian Refugee Council](https://www.nrc.no/), where I work on quantifying the socio-economic impacts of forced displacement across more than 200 countries and territories worldwide.

</div>

</div>

<br>
<span style="font-weight:700; font-size:1.25em;"> A glimpse of my research</span>

My research integrates statistical models, machine learning algorithms, and data science techniques to advance our understanding of _how individuals, families, and communities experience, adapt to, and cope with complex phenomena such as armed conflict, violence, climate change, poverty, and forced displacement_. Through the application of cutting-edge methods to these phenomena, my work contributes to an emerging scientific field that I refer to as **_computational humanitarian research_**.

Another line of my research focuses on enhancing knowledge of [disease outbreaks](https://jatorresmunguia.github.io/disease-outbreaks-data.github.io/) by improving the availability and quality of data and promoting analyses to identify geospatial trends and patterns worldwide. In this research area, I am the author of [_A global dataset of pandemic- and epidemic-prone disease outbreaks_](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41597-022-01797-2), which is integrated into the [_Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX)_](https://data.humdata.org/dataset/global-pandemic-and-epidemic-outbreaks) initiative of the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA).

More recently, I have applied boosting for structured additive regression models, which combine model interpretability with predictive performance, to investigate development and humanitarian outcomes associated with armed conflict and climate change. Three main research questions guide this work: **(1)** _How do armed conflict and climate change jointly contribute to the emergence of humanitarian [_polycrises_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polycrisis)?_ **(2)** _Does the interaction between armed conflict and climate change disproportionately expose certain population groups to humanitarian crises?_ and **(3)** _How can we predict whether, how, where, and when these polycrises may occur in the future?_. Feel free to [send me a message](../contact/index.qmd) if you are interested in this line of work.

Check out my [publications](../publications/index.qmd) to learn more about my research.

<span style="font-weight:700; font-size:1.25em;"> Brief summary of my professional experience</span>

I have contributed to research projects analyzing data related to humanitarian crises, development, and vulnerable populations, working with several international organizations, including the Norwegian Refugee Council, the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime, the United Nations Institute for Disarmament Research, the International Organization for Migration, and UN Women.

My work has covered a wide range of topics and geographical contexts, including the Boko Haram insurgency in the Lake Chad Basin (Nigeria, Cameroon, Chad, and Niger); ISIS in Iraq; armed guerrilla groups in Colombia; urban violence in Latin America; conflict-induced displacement in Sudan; disaster-induced displacement in Bangladesh, Kenya, Nigeria, and Guatemala; geospatial analysis of femicides in Mexico; and migration governance in Central America and the Caribbean.

See my [CV](../cv/index.qmd) for more details.
